knowledge:
- key_parameters: cy3=Column index for Cy3 intensity in read.spot ;; cy5=Column index for Cy5 intensity in read.spot ;; bg.cy3=Column index for Cy3 background in read.spot ;; bg.cy5=Column index for Cy5 background in read.spot ;; ids=Column index for gene identifiers in read.spot ;; nr=Number of rows in each subgrid for grid.norm ;; nc=Number of columns in each subgrid for grid.norm ;; type=Type of Z-score analysis, either "ri" (R-I plot) or "ma" (M-A plot) ;; Zscore.min=Minimum Z-score threshold for plotting in Zscore.plot ;; output.file=Output file name for genMerge results
- alternatives: imageLimma is completely based on the imageplot function from the limma package ;; genMerge is completely based on GeneMerge by Cristian I. Castillo-Davis and Daniel L. Hartl
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing raw dual-color (two-channel) microarray data to perform background correction, normalization, replicate filtering, and identify differentially expressed genes using Z-scores.
- pitfalls: Grid normalization (grid.norm) can only be applied to the complete dataset, so spots must not be eliminated before running it ;; If spots are eliminated before normalization, global.norm is the only valid normalization option ;; In the normalization procedure, any observation where the R value is zero will be eliminated ;; Input files for genMerge must not have a header row ;; post.analysis requires a list of files with .prj extension and can only be used if results were obtained via the genArise GUI

workflows.name: dual_color_microarray_analysis
workflows.intent: Preprocess raw dual-color microarray data, perform background correction, normalize, filter low-quality spots, resolve replicates, and identify differentially expressed genes using Z-scores.
input: raw_intensities.txt (tab-delimited file containing Cy3/Cy5 intensities, backgrounds, and gene IDs)
workflows.stages: 1. Read raw data using read.spot ;; 2. Perform background correction using bg.correct ;; 3. Normalize data using grid.norm or global.norm ;; 4. Filter low-quality spots using filter.spot ;; 5. Handle replicate spots using spotUnique, alter.unique, or meanUnique ;; 6. Calculate Z-scores using Zscore ;; 7. Plot diagnostic and Z-score plots using imageLimma, ri.plot, ma.plot, cys.plot, and Zscore.plot
workflows.code:
my.spot <- read.spot( file.name, cy3 = 1, cy5 = 2, bg.cy3 = 3, bg.cy5 = 4, ids = 5, header = FALSE, sep = "\t", is.ifc = FALSE)
data(Simon)
datos <- attr(Simon, "spotData")
M <- log(datos$Cy3, 2) - log(datos$Cy5, 2)
imageLimma(z = M, row = 23, column = 24, meta.row = 2, meta.column = 2, low = NULL, high = NULL)
R <- log(datos$BgCy3, 2)
imageLimma(z = R, row = 23, column = 24, meta.row = 2, meta.column = 2, low = "white", high = "red")
G <- log(datos$BgCy5, 2)
imageLimma(z = G, row = 23, column = 24, meta.row = 2, meta.column = 2, low = "white", high = "green")
ri.plot(Simon)
ma.plot(Simon)
cys.plot(Simon)
c.spot <- bg.correct(Simon)
n.spot <- grid.norm(mySpot = Simon, nr = 23, nc = 24)
n.spot <- global.norm(mySpot = Simon)
f.spot <- filter.spot(mySpot = Simon)
u.spot <- spotUnique(mySpot = Simon)
u.spot <- alter.unique(mySpot = Simon)
u.spot <- meanUnique(mySpot = Simon)
s.spot <- Zscore(Simon, type="ri")
s.spot <- Zscore(Simon, type="ma")
data(WT.dataset)
Zscore.plot(WT.dataset, Zscore.min=1)

workflows.name: functional_enrichment_genmerge
workflows.intent: Perform functional genomic annotation and statistical over-representation analysis of differentially expressed genes.
input: population.genes (file containing all gene IDs in the microarray)
study.genes (file containing the study gene IDs, e.g., up- or down-regulated)
workflows.stages: 1. Extract population gene IDs and write to file using write.table ;; 2. Extract study gene IDs (up-regulated, down-regulated, or both) and write to file using write.table ;; 3. Run over-representation analysis using genMerge
workflows.code:
ids <- attr(o.spot, "spotData")$Ids
ids <- unique(ids)
write.table(ids, "population.genes")
study.ids <- c(s.spot$Id.up, s.spot$Id.down)
study.ids <- unique(study.ids)
write.table(study.ids, "study.genes")
study.ids <- s.spot$Id.up
study.ids <- unique(study.ids)
write.table(study.ids, "study.genes")
genMerge(gene.association, description, population.genes, study.genes, output.file = "GeneMerge.txt")
